# Jhānantarikakathā (Kv 18.7)

**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jhānantarikakathā* (Kv 18.7) is a doctrinal controversy preserved in the eighteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The text examines the proposition that there exist intermediate stages between meditative absorptions (*jhānantarika*) [Bareau 1955; Dube 1980]. André Bareau records this thesis as maintained by branches of the Andhakas, who affirmed intermediate meditative states between consecutive *jhānas* [Bareau 1955]. S. N. Dube observes that the advocacy of *jhānantarika* is attributed to the Sammatīyas in counterpoint to the thesis of *jhāna-saṅkamati*, and notes that the commentator Buddhaghosa explicitly distinguished this sectarian view from the orthodox Theravāda fivefold *jhāna* scheme [Dube 1980].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in: DN 34 (PTS DN iii 272) Dasuttara Sutta; Kv 9.7 Vitakkānupatitakathā

**Sources**

- [Dube 1980] S. N. Dube, Cross Currents in Early Buddhism (1980) — Discussion of the Sammatīya thesis of intermediate meditative stages (jhānantarika) and Buddhaghosa's distinction from the Theravāda five-jhāna scheme.
- [Bareau 1955] André Bareau, Les sectes bouddhiques du Petit Véhicule (1955) — Attribution of the thesis of intermediate stages between jhānas to certain Andhaka groups.
